name: Forcepoint DLP — Bulk Sensitive Data to Personal / Public Email by One User
description:
Attacker objective
Mass-exfiltrate sensitive data by emailing many distinct sensitive documents to a personal or public webmail account within a short window — a classic pre-departure or insider data theft.

Attack logic
A single sensitive email to a personal address may be incidental; one user sending several distinct sensitive documents to public-mail domains in a short window is deliberate bulk exfiltration.

Why this detection works
Aggregating distinct deduplicated DLP incidents (by incident ID) per user, scoped to sensitive content to public-mail domains, separates bulk exfiltration from the occasional single message.

False positives
A user with a legitimate one-off bulk task (e.g. an authorised transfer to a partner on a public domain).

Tuning
Raise the per-user incident threshold to the local routine rate; allowlist sanctioned bulk-processing/service accounts; review the document list and recipients.

Required telemetry
Forcepoint DLP CEF: eventId (incident dedup key), deviceEventCategory, loginName, destinationUserName, filename.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the user's distinct sensitive documents and recipients listed in the alert.
2. Confirm whether this is authorised bulk business or insider exfiltration; correlate with HR/leaver status where available.
3. Escalate to fraud/compliance and consider disabling the account pending investigation.
false_positives: A user with a legitimate one-off bulk task (e.g. an authorised transfer to a partner on a public domain).
query:
FROM logs-cef.log-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*"
| WHERE cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive words*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*")
| EVAL user.name = TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\")))
| STATS incidents = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.extensions.eventId), recipients = VALUES(cef.extensions.destinationUserName), files = VALUES(cef.extensions.filename), hosts = VALUES(cef.extensions.sourceHost) BY user.name
| WHERE incidents >= 3

name: Forcepoint DLP — Cardholder / PCI Data Transfer
description:
Attacker objective
Exfiltrate regulated cardholder / payment-card (PCI) data out of the bank via email, web upload, print or removable media.

Attack logic
The DLP engine classifies content against a payment-card (PCI) data classifier. A transfer that matches this classifier means regulated cardholder data was moving through a monitored channel — the highest-value data-loss event for a bank.

Why this detection works
The PCI content classifier is a structured, high-precision label; any transfer carrying it is inherently sensitive and warrants review regardless of channel or severity.

False positives
Authorised card-operations staff handling cardholder data as part of their role; an internal transfer to a sanctioned system.

Tuning
Allowlist verified card-operations workflows and internal sanctioned destinations; prioritise transfers to external destinations (personal email, web upload, USB).

Required telemetry
Forcepoint DLP CEF: deviceEventCategory (data classifier), sourceServiceName (channel), loginName/sourceHost (user/endpoint), destinationHosts/destinationUserName (destination).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the user (loginName), endpoint (sourceHost), channel (sourceServiceName) and destination.
2. Confirm whether the destination is external and whether the transfer was authorised card-operations work.
3. Treat cardholder data leaving to an external/personal destination as a data-breach incident — escalate to fraud/compliance.
false_positives: Authorised card-operations staff handling cardholder data as part of their role; an internal transfer to a sanctioned system.
query:
FROM logs-cef.log-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*"
| EVAL host.name = CASE(cef.extensions.sourceHost != "N/A" AND cef.extensions.sourceHost IS NOT NULL, TO_LOWER(MV_FIRST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.sourceHost, "."))), null), source.ip = CASE(cef.extensions.sourceIp != "N/A" AND cef.extensions.sourceIp IS NOT NULL, TO_IP(cef.extensions.sourceIp), null), user.name = CASE(cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*", TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))), null)
| KEEP @timestamp, host.name, source.ip, user.name, cef.extensions.loginName, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName, cef.extensions.destinationHosts, cef.extensions.destinationUserName, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.eventId

name: Forcepoint DLP — High Severity Policy Match
Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Sent to a Personal / Public Email Domain
description:
Attacker objective
Exfiltrate sensitive corporate data by emailing it to a personal or public webmail account (e.g. a free consumer email domain) the attacker or insider controls.

Attack logic
The DLP engine flags recipients on public/personal email domains and, separately, sensitive content. An event carrying both a public-mail-domain classifier and a sensitive-content classifier is sensitive data leaving to a personal mailbox.

Why this detection works
Combining the public-mail-domain classifier with a sensitive-content classifier isolates genuine data leakage from routine external business email (which is not sensitive) and internal mail.

False positives
An employee legitimately sending non-critical work to their own personal address; a business contact on a webmail domain.

Tuning
Escalate users with repeated or bulk occurrences; allowlist sanctioned business partners on public domains; review the file and recipient.

Required telemetry
Forcepoint DLP CEF: deviceEventCategory (Public Mail Domain + sensitive classifier), destinationUserName (recipient), loginName (sender), filename.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the recipient (destinationUserName), the file (filename) and the classifier.
2. Confirm whether the recipient is a personal account of the sender and whether the content is genuinely sensitive.
3. Repeated sensitive sends to personal email indicate insider exfiltration — involve HR/compliance.
false_positives: An employee legitimately sending non-critical work to their own personal address; a business contact on a webmail domain.
query:
FROM logs-cef.log-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Public Mail Domain*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive Words-Outbound*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*")
| EVAL host.name = CASE(cef.extensions.sourceHost != "N/A" AND cef.extensions.sourceHost IS NOT NULL, TO_LOWER(MV_FIRST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.sourceHost, "."))), null), source.ip = CASE(cef.extensions.sourceIp != "N/A" AND cef.extensions.sourceIp IS NOT NULL, TO_IP(cef.extensions.sourceIp), null), user.name = CASE(cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*", TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))), null)
| KEEP @timestamp, host.name, source.ip, user.name, cef.extensions.loginName, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName, cef.extensions.destinationHosts, cef.extensions.destinationUserName, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.eventId

name: Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Transfer Outside Working Hours
description:
Attacker objective
Move sensitive data at an unusual time — outside the user's normal working hours — to reduce the chance of being observed, a common insider-exfiltration and compromised-account pattern.

Attack logic
The DLP engine flags transfers occurring outside expected working hours. Combined with a sensitive-content classifier, an out-of-hours sensitive transfer is a higher-risk event than the same transfer during business hours.

Why this detection works
Using the DLP engine's own out-of-hours classifier together with a sensitive-content classifier avoids fragile local time-window logic and isolates sensitive data moving at anomalous times.

False positives
Shift workers, on-call staff, or automated jobs that legitimately run outside business hours.

Tuning
Allowlist verified out-of-hours business processes and service accounts; prioritise interactive users and external destinations.

Required telemetry
Forcepoint DLP CEF: deviceEventCategory (Data Sent During Unusual Hours + sensitive classifier), loginName, sourceHost, destinationHosts/destinationUserName.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Confirm the user's normal working pattern and whether an out-of-hours sensitive transfer is expected.
2. Review the destination and file; an out-of-hours sensitive transfer to an external destination is high-risk.
3. Correlate with the user's authentication activity for signs of account compromise.
false_positives: Shift workers, on-call staff, or automated jobs that legitimately run outside business hours.
query:
FROM logs-cef.log-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE observer.vendor == "Forcepoint" AND cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Unusual Hours*" AND (cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Sensitive words*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*PCI*" OR cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory LIKE "*Files Outbound*")
| EVAL host.name = CASE(cef.extensions.sourceHost != "N/A" AND cef.extensions.sourceHost IS NOT NULL, TO_LOWER(MV_FIRST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.sourceHost, "."))), null), source.ip = CASE(cef.extensions.sourceIp != "N/A" AND cef.extensions.sourceIp IS NOT NULL, TO_IP(cef.extensions.sourceIp), null), user.name = CASE(cef.extensions.loginName LIKE "INTDOM*", TO_LOWER(MV_LAST(SPLIT(cef.extensions.loginName, "\\"))), null)
| KEEP @timestamp, host.name, source.ip, user.name, cef.extensions.loginName, cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory, cef.extensions.sourceServiceName, cef.extensions.destinationHosts, cef.extensions.destinationUserName, cef.extensions.filename, cef.extensions.eventId

name: Forcepoint DLP — Sensitive Data Uploaded to a New External Web Destination
description:
Attacker objective
Exfiltrate sensitive data by uploading it over the web to a new external destination — a personal cloud-storage account, file-sharing site, or other service not previously used.

Attack logic
Users upload data to a stable set of sanctioned web destinations. The first time sensitive content is uploaded to a destination not seen before is a candidate exfiltration or shadow-IT event.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over the web destination auto-baselines the organisation's normal upload destinations and fires only when sensitive content goes to a genuinely new one.

False positives
Adoption of a new legitimate SaaS/cloud service; a new business partner portal.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned new destinations after review; scope to higher-value classifiers if the volume of new SaaS destinations is high.

Required telemetry
Forcepoint DLP CEF (web channels): destinationHosts (upload destination), sourceServiceName (channel), deviceEventCategory (sensitive classifier), loginName.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify the new destination (destinationHosts), the user and the sensitive content.
2. Determine whether the destination is a sanctioned service or personal cloud storage / file-sharing site.
3. If unsanctioned, treat as exfiltration/shadow-IT and review what data reached it.
false_positives: Adoption of a new legitimate SaaS/cloud service; a new business partner portal.
query: observer.vendor:"Forcepoint" and cef.extensions.sourceServiceName:(*Content Gateway* or *Endpoint HTTPS* or *Endpoint Web*) and cef.extensions.deviceEventCategory:(*Sensitive words* or *PCI* or *Files Outbound* or *Sensitive Words-Outbound*) and cef.extensions.destinationHosts:* and not cef.extensions.destinationHosts:"N/A"
